<thought>We need to provide a list of SMILES fragments that can be joined to form the target molecule (C14H12O6, DBE 9, 12 unique carbon environments, 11 aromatic carbons, one CH₃, one carbonyl). The 13C NMR shows signals for an ethyl ester (CH₃ ~14 ppm, CH₂‑O ~61 ppm, carbonyl ~166 ppm) and an aromatic ring with four phenolic OH groups (multiple aromatic carbons around 116‑151 ppm). A suitable fragmentation is:
1. Ethyl‑ester fragment: CCOC(=O) (contains the CH₃, CH₂‑O, and carbonyl carbon).
2. Tetra‑hydroxy‑phenyl fragment: c1c(O)cc(O)cc(O)c1O (a benzene ring bearing four OH groups; provides the remaining aromatic carbons and oxygens).

These two fragments together give C14H12O6 and satisfy all given constraints. Both SMILES are valid.
